quick_english: I become the universal fire, abiding in the bodies of living beings, joined with prāṇa and apāna, and cook the fourfold food. The venerable teachers say that the world-sustaining power of the five elements, as whole and part, is the Lord's māheśvarya. The sun's light illuminates and sustains; the moon's light illuminates and nourishes herbs; fire's light illuminates, dries, burns, sweats, and cooks; and space is all-pervading as awareness-space. Therefore, having stated the knowable form, he shows the self as supreme Lord, all-knowing, independent, and all-maker.

quick_english: I dwell in the heart of all; from me come memory, knowledge, and removal. I alone am known by all the Vedas and Vedanta. The knowable nature is independent knowing, and the reflection 'there I am' is knowledge as new manifestation and world-creation. Conceptual knowledge is removal, bond-creation, and maya-made fixation; remembering is the residue of withdrawn impressions manifesting again. Thus all knowledges are withdrawn, and agency as freedom preceded by omniscience is declared. All scriptures determine the supreme Lord-principle alone; the Lord's freedom is world-agency through creating, uprooting, and re-establishing own nature. Others, by difference-cognition, make removal and thereby produce Vedanta and Veda through self-realization.

quick_english: Because I transcend both the perishable and the imperishable, I am supreme; therefore I am renowned in the world and in the Veda as the supreme person. The text says there are these two persons in the world. Even in an unawakened state, people know the conscious self with a body made of elements as perishable form, and from the world's delusion the dualistic view does not cease. But I, all-gracious, split the dualistic knot and, pervading all the world, am to be known. I transcend the perishable because beings are inert, and the imperishable because all-pervasion is denied in the unawakened self. Thus, by explanations beginning with the supreme person in world and Veda, he alone is said to be the supreme nondual self.
